reason: Both conversations correctly identify tE as a heating/thermistor fault, keep the user safe (unplug first / don't open the casing) and escalate to an engineer, but Conversation 1 adapts far better once the homeowner reveals he can't move the machine or test anything: it addresses the key unknown of warranty status (LG promo cover, retailer rights, insurance), gives realistic repair costs, a ready-made description for the engineer, and sensible interim advice to use only cold/30 washes. Conversation 2 is efficient and safe but ends with a bare 'call an engineer', never raising warranty or age, offering no interim guidance, and leaning somewhat confidently on the thermistor under its heading. Conversation 1's slight overreach (initial DIY meter instructions, and later naming the heater as most likely) is tempered by its repeated insistence that an engineer confirm with a meter before parts are fitted.
